annotation.title_clean: On the Role of Beliefs and Trust for the Intention to Use Service Robots: An Integrated Trustworthiness Beliefs Model for Robot Acceptance
annotation.title_en: On the Role of Beliefs and Trust for the Intention to Use Service Robots: An Integrated Trustworthiness Beliefs Model for Robot Acceptance
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kraus, J.; Miller, L.; Klumpp, M.; Babel, F.; Scholz, D.; Merger, J.; et al.
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed online study (N=400) proposing the Trustworthiness Beliefs Robot Acceptance Model (TB-RAM), integrating UTAUT, trust and Theory of Planned Behavior beliefs to predict intention to use service robots. Finds trust mediates beliefs to intention; competence, effort expectancy and social influence matter. Not a governance document.
key_provisions_or_claims: General trust in service robots is a starting point for trust in a specific robot.
Trust mediates the effect of beliefs on intention to use robots.
Competence and effort expectancy predict general trust; competence and social influence predict trust in a specific robot.
Social influence effect on trust is stronger in public than private application areas.
Distinct beliefs improve explanatory value of acceptance models over broad ones.
